inspection_summary: Inspected all 559 normalized lines. The usable mathematical core develops the Baez-Duarte sequence and its Riesz generating-function bridge, documents the catastrophic-cancellation barrier in direct evaluation, decomposes the sequence into trend and zero-driven oscillation, derives asymptotic wave structure and low-zero dominance, and explains why numerical nonviolation is a weak detector of hypothetical off-critical zeros. The two-column extraction interleaves some prose, formulas, tables, and references; units retain the exact spans needed to keep the recoverable arguments auditable and flag formula dependence.

accepted_units.title: Baez-Duarte decay criterion and exponential generating identity
accepted_units.why_material: The frozen v1 span states the equivalence between RH and the k^{-3/4+epsilon} decay threshold, notes the sharpness and simple-zero strengthening, and introduces the inversion/generating-function framing that makes the sequence analytically useful.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit. Its displayed identity continues beyond line 74 and the actual definition of c_k follows at lines 75-86, so interpretation requires the recorded v1 context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: two-column extraction interleaves prose and displayed equations; the conceptual claims are recoverable, but exact formula typography should be checked against the scan before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.unit_type: representation bridge and equivalent growth criterion
accepted_units.title: Finite-difference sequence as an exponential transform of the Riesz function
accepted_units.why_material: The passage defines c_k, places it in a general binomial/exponential-transform identity, identifies its generating function with R(x)/x, and states the bidirectional correspondence R(x)=O(x^{delta+1}) iff c_k=O(k^delta). This is the source's main bridge from a discrete sequence to an analytic growth criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes interleaved right-column material about early sign changes and a cancellation table because the normalized page is two-column; the sequence-to-Riesz chain is nevertheless recoverable across equations (1), (4), and (7)-(9).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact exponents, factorials, and summation indices are formula-layer dependent, although the surrounding prose explicitly states the transform and growth equivalence.

accepted_units.title: Catastrophic cancellation forces precision linear in the sequence index
accepted_units.why_material: Direct evaluation combines enormous alternating partial sums to obtain tiny c_k values. The paper turns that instability into a concrete precision rule, requiring enough digits to distinguish 1 from 1+2^{-k}, and uses the generic formula as a slow computation that does not assume RH, hence as an independent check on fast zero-based formulas.
accepted_units.context_note: The span crosses the Computer Experiments heading and a page boundary so that the partial-sum evidence, PARI/GP procedure, failure example, precision rule, and methodological comparison remain together.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: the prose and precision mechanism are clear, while table exponents, code layout, and finite-difference notation remain vulnerable to extraction errors.

accepted_units.title: Separating a rapidly decaying trend from zero-driven oscillation
accepted_units.why_material: The explicit formulas recast c_k as a trend plus an oscillatory sum over nontrivial zeta zeros, state the simple-zero assumption, and contrast the fast assumption-dependent route with the generic formula. The unexpectedly good small-k agreement is used only as numerical evidence that omitted integrals decay rapidly.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 199-207 also contain the final interleaved computer-experiment paragraph; retaining them supplies the method comparison that motivates the explicit-formula section.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (10)-(11), the beta/gamma ratios, primes on zeta, and zero indexing require scan verification before exact computational use.

accepted_units.title: Trend/oscillation representation and its asymptotic regime
accepted_units.why_material: The immutable v1 span contains the assumptions on the zero sum, identifies the beta-function representation, reports close agreement with the generic sequence, and begins the exact-to-asymptotic treatment of the trend. It preserves the conceptual split between smooth decay and spectral fluctuation.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit. The decomposition and zero-sum equations begin at lines 199-242, while the oscillatory interpretation and coefficient decay continue through line 364; both sides are required by the recorded repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the span begins and ends amid displayed formulas in a two-column extraction, so it is not safe as a self-contained symbolic transcription.

accepted_units.title: The trend is asymptotically k^{-2}, below the criterion-scale wave
accepted_units.why_material: The source derives an exact trend series, a finite asymptotic expansion, and a leading k^{-2} simplification, then compares all three across increasing k. This establishes that the trend decays faster than the k^{-3/4} oscillatory scale relevant to the criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison table is retained because it shows where the successive approximations become reliable rather than merely listing outputs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact constants and correction terms are embedded in extraction-fragile displays; the asymptotic ordering and table trend are recoverable from the checked prose and rows.

accepted_units.title: Conjugate zeros generate logarithmic waves with exponentially damped coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming RH, conjugate zeros convert the oscillatory term into a k^{-3/4} envelope multiplying sines and cosines whose log(k) frequencies are set by zero ordinates. The Hadamard-product and gamma-identity discussion yields exponential coefficient decay, explaining why only the first few zeros materially shape the computed wave.
accepted_units.context_note: The span overlaps the trend unit to retain the assumption and asymptotic beta-function step that lead into equation (16), then includes the coefficient argument and Table 4 evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the conceptual frequency/amplitude separation is prose-supported, but equation (16), alpha/beta definitions, and exponential factors must be scan-verified before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: First-zero dominance turns the normalized sequence into a log-periodic sine
accepted_units.why_material: The first-zero truncation rewrites k^{3/4}c_k as a single phase-shifted sinusoid with constant wavelength on a logarithmic k-axis. Consecutive sign changes then estimate the first zero's ordinate, while a Mobius-sum transform supplies the independent c_k calculation required for that check.
accepted_units.context_note: The normalized two-column page interleaves the wave derivation, transformed formula, and sign-change table. Keeping the full span preserves both the proposed diagnostic and the author's explicit independence requirement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: formula (26), phase conventions, the ratio in formula (25), and table columns are extraction-sensitive; the stated log-periodic mechanism and independence condition are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Off-critical zeros may be invisible because spectral damping overwhelms asymptotic growth
accepted_units.why_material: The immutable v1 span separates on-line and hypothetical off-line zero contributions and argues that a very high off-line zero could have an exponentially tiny coefficient, requiring an enormous k before its slower-decaying contribution becomes visible. This directly limits what finite nonviolation of the decay bound can establish.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 unit. It relies on the earlier explicit wave formula, coefficient damping, and first-zero reduction, so the repair extends back to line 278. The estimates for hypothetical zeros are heuristic and are presented as such by the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the obstruction is clear in prose, but the extracted powers and exponential factors should be scan-checked before quantitative citation.

accepted_units.title: Fast arbitrary-index evaluation is not visibly destabilized by the first Lehmer pair
accepted_units.why_material: The final remarks state that the low-zero explicit formula enables evaluation at arbitrary large indices and contrast the Baez-Duarte bound with criteria sensitive to Lehmer pairs. The checked first pair has derivative values comparable for its two zeros, so the author finds no mechanism there for violating the bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Reference entries are interleaved with the left-column final remarks, but the mathematical prose from the heading through the derivative comparison remains readable. This is numerical evidence and a method-specific comparison, not a proof of robustness for all pairs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: formula references and derivative values are extraction-sensitive, while the qualitative comparison is prose-supported.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Discrete-to-analytic growth transfer
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The binomially defined sequence and the Riesz function are linked by an exponential generating transform whose growth-rate equivalence turns the same RH threshold into discrete decay or analytic growth.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The normalized formulas are extraction-fragile, and the source reports the equivalence rather than reproducing its proof.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Spectral wave structure and the observational bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A k^{-2} trend becomes negligible beside a k^{-3/4} zero-driven wave; exponential damping makes the first zero dominate observed oscillation while also making a sufficiently high hypothetical off-line zero extraordinarily hard to detect at finite k.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The displayed oscillatory asymptotic assumes RH and simple zeros, while the damping estimate for hypothetical off-line zeros is explicitly heuristic.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Assumption-independent computation as a control
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The slow generic finite-difference computation, despite severe precision cost, does not assume RH and therefore controls fast explicit zero-based calculations and sign-change diagnostics that do use stronger assumptions or approximations.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Agreement over computed ranges validates numerical implementation conditionally; it neither proves the asymptotic criterion nor excludes later violations.

within_source_saturation: Whole-source saturation was reached after representing every distinct mechanism supported by the readable text: criterion and transform, direct-computation instability, explicit decomposition, trend hierarchy, spectral damping, first-mode diagnostics, finite-observation obstruction, and the final criterion comparison. Remaining tables either serve these selected mechanisms, while repeated summaries, references, biography, headers, and extraction-only fragments add no new semantic move.
stop_reason: All 559 frozen lines were inspected and assigned a coverage disposition. Beyond the ten accepted units, the source contains only supporting page structure, repeated numerical displays already tied to selected mechanisms, bibliography/front matter, and author biography; further segmentation would duplicate represented arguments or isolate formula fragments made unsafe by the two-column extraction.
